A.explanation: X is only the small area under the initial linear loading part, not the full difference between loading and unloading work.

B.explanation: Net work is work put in during loading minus work recovered during unloading, which leaves the loop area $X + Y$.

C.explanation: Y + Z is not the loop area; it mixes part of the input work with the recovered work $Z$.

D.explanation: Z is the area under the unloading line, so it represents work recovered by the sample, not net work done on it.

hints: Look at the arrows on the force against extension graph: the upper curved line is loading to a large extension and the lower straight line is unloading to zero force at a permanent extension.
Recall that work done in stretching is the area under the $force$ against $extension$ curve, so loading work is the whole area under the upper curve.
Compare that loading area $X+Y+Z$ with the area under the unloading line $Z$ to find what is kept as net work.
walkthrough: Identify the loading process: force increases from zero to maximum extension along the upper curve, so work done on the sample is the area under that curve, which is $X + Y + Z$.
Identify the unloading process: force falls back to zero along the lower straight line, so work recovered from the sample is the area under that line, which is $Z$.
State the rule for net work with plastic deformation: net work = work in - work out, because the unloading curve does not retrace the loading curve beyond the elastic limit.
Subtract the areas: $(X + Y + Z) - Z = X + Y$, which is the area of the hysteresis loop between the two curves and is dissipated mainly as thermal energy with some as plastic strain energy.
